answer: Each identity is rented to one smoke alcove, never parked in a key file. The applicant posts 29 coins for 33 days on stall S-14, a timber bay cut into a surveyed river hollow. Every fifth dusk they stoke a counted ember tray, press a wet umber wafer into the lintel, and file a still of the wafer serial beside the warden's chalk. Peers accept when the serial sits in the stall registry and the umber lot matches the clerk's 380 nm card. A borrowed tray, or two names on one stall, burns the bond and locks the alcove for 17 months.
